source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of inspection.
3. Clearly note the specific areas or components of the building that failed the fire-safety check.
4. Provide detailed observations: describe the nature of the failure (e.g., malfunctioning smoke alarm, blocked fire exits, lack of emergency lighting, etc.). 
5. Take photographs or videos to visually document the issues (include timestamps).
6. Document any conversations or communications related to the failed checks, including with building management, occupants, or other authorities.
7. Write down any immediate actions or recommendations you suggested to rectify the issue (e.g., repair, replacement, further investigation).
8. If applicable, note the fire-safety standards or codes that were violated (include reference numbers or section titles).
9. Record the presence or input of other professionals if applicable (e.g., fire marshals, building inspectors).
10. Complete a standardized form or checklist if required by your organization, including all relevant information
